title: ID0484922-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP/S3 170003383] ELMS Unable to ping
description:
Reported behavior/issue: Customer is trying to connect 2 devices at same time and causes one to crash → not charger related
Solution: Don't use 2 devices at the same time, ELMS is working.

Hi,
ELMS seems still to be able to read from the Sicharge.
I suspect that when I try to read with a 3th device from Sicharge, the modbus communication will stop, but I’m not able to test this now.
Last time we had this timeline:
Sicharge boots up, together with ELMS, communication works OK.
I try to read with modbus tool from my laptop (3th device), but connection gets refused.
At same time the already established communication between ELMS and Sicharge also stops working.
Last time I was not able to solve this with a cloud hard-reboot, I needed to power cycle the complete device to get it working again.
So this means that it wil probably work now, as long we don’t try to connect with 3th device…

additional_info.subject: ID0484922-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP/S3 170003383] Unable to ping CRM:02889001325
additional_info.body:
Hi Nico, good morning.
Thanks for the feedback.
I'm not quite sure I understood your architecture, but you mention that you are connecting a 3rd device to the same Sicharge D?
If yes, that is impossible due to the Modbus protocol constraints, only one device can use a modbus port at the same time, the next devices get refused.
When you get that connected refused it's completely normal, that is also our usual test to make sure that the ELMS is also working from your side, I create a virtual ELMS in our charger and if the connection gets refused, it means that the ELMS is connected to our charger.
I will wait for your feedback.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0484922-DC/Si-D/BE-[MP/S3 170003383] Unable to ping CRM:02889001325
additional_info.body:
Hi Nico, good morning.
Thanks for the feedback.
What I don't understand from your emails is the architecture of the system, can you please explain to me, step by step what you are doing? From what I understand I am assuming it's something similar to either Plan1 or Plan2
Plan1:
step 1 - Physical connection from Sicharge D is coming to a Ethernet switch and ELMS is connected
step 2 - connect your laptop to a free port
step 3 - run Modbus tool software
step 4 - ELMS and SiD communication gets dropped
Plan2:
step 1 - Remove the physical connection from SiD to ELMS and bring it to laptop
step 2 - run Modbus tool software
step 3 - reconnect ELMS and not possible anymore.
Or another plan.
Can you please enlighten me on this? The reason why I need this, is to try my best to reproduce your error in my test charger and confirm that behaviour.
I will wait for your feedback.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco
